projects.name: Postiz (gitroomhq/postiz-app)
projects.license: AGPL-3.0 (verified on repo page). Cloud SaaS also offered.
projects.model: Self-hosted web app (Next.js/NestJS, PostgreSQL via Prisma + Redis, Docker) or managed Postiz Cloud. No native mobile/desktop app; no share-sheet hand-off or 'notification publishing' documented (llms.txt index has no manual-posting/mobile pages).
projects.networks: X, Instagram (Facebook-Business and Standalone), Threads, TikTok, LinkedIn + LinkedIn Page, Facebook Page, YouTube, Pinterest, Reddit, Discord, Slack, Mastodon, Bluesky, Dribbble, Farcaster, Nostr, Lemmy, Medium, Dev.to, Hashnode, WordPress, Listmonk, Google My Business, Skool, Moltbook (docs.postiz.com/providers index, read 2026-10-07).
projects.restricted_network_strategy: BYO developer app, but INSTANCE-wide not per-user: self-hoster registers one app per platform and puts keys in env vars (X_API_KEY/X_API_SECRET, FACEBOOK_APP_ID, INSTAGRAM_APP_ID, THREADS_APP_ID, MASTODON_CLIENT_ID...). Only Bluesky, Lemmy, Nostr, Medium, Dev.to, Hashnode, WordPress, Listmonk, Moltbook, Skool need no developer app (credentials typed in the UI). Verified from docs + source: X = OAuth 1.0a via twitter-api-v2, app must be 'Native App' type with Read+Write (other app types fail with error 32), posts via POST /2/tweets, chunked media via /media/upload initialize/append/finalize, maxLength 280 or 4000 if the account was detected 'Verified', 429 -> retry with 5s*attempt backoff, 'not permitted' -> bad_body. Bluesky = app password via BskyAgent.login() with user-supplied custom PDS URL (validated as public HTTPS), 300-char cap, RichText.detectFacets(), images resized down to ~976KB, max 4 images / 1 video, arm-confirm-publish handshake to avoid duplicate posts. Mastodon = self-hoster registers an app per instance with curl and sets MASTODON_URL. Instagram = Meta 'Business' app with advanced access to instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish etc.; 'For public applications, you will need to verify your business'; Standalone needs a professional IG account. Threads = threads_basic + threads_content_publish, docs say no extra review needed. TikTok = unaudited app forced to SELF_ONLY (private) posts, max 5 users/24h, media must be publicly reachable over HTTPS, HTTPS redirect required. LinkedIn = must add 'Advertising API' product and fill its request form or token refresh will not work. Cloud tier sells 'pre-approved apps for every channel' as the differentiator; README warns self-host approvals 'can take weeks'.
projects.active: Very active: 36.9k stars, 3,301 commits, issues filed through Sep 2026 (verified 2026-10-07).

projects.name: Mixpost (inovector/mixpost)
projects.license: Lite = MIT (verified); Pro ($299 one-time) and Enterprise ($1,199 one-time) are commercial; Pro license forbids building a SaaS (mixpost.app/pricing).
projects.model: Self-hosted Laravel/PHP web app (Docker, manual PHP, or Laravel package); Mixpost Cloud also offered. Docs require a public domain ('will not work with localhost or any private network addresses').
projects.networks: Lite: Facebook Pages, X, Mastodon only. Pro/Enterprise add Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Google Business Profile.
projects.restricted_network_strategy: BYO developer app configured ONCE per instance in Admin Console > Services ('required only once per application'), then each user OAuths their account. X page (read 2026-10-07): sign up on the X Developer Portal selecting the 'Pay as you go' plan, create a Production app, use OAuth 1.0a keys, app permission Read and write, app type 'Web App, Automated App or Bot', callback https://example.com/<MIXPOST_CORE_PATH>/callback/twitter; a separate 'legacy' guide exists for the old free tier. Mixpost adds cost-control knobs for X: analytics history (full/30d/7d/off), engagement reads on/off, and posts-with-links per thread (unlimited / none / 1-10). Instagram Standalone: Meta use case 'Manage messaging & content on Instagram', scopes instagram_business_content_publish/_manage_comments/_manage_insights, only Professional (Business/Creator) accounts, 'Until your app is published, only Instagram accounts added as testers can connect', then app review for advanced access. Bluesky (Pro only): admin 'Generate new private key' in dashboard + public domain required (reads like an OAuth client key, not an app password - mechanism not confirmed).
projects.active: Active: 3.8k stars, issues through Jun 2026 (incl. #204 reflected-XSS via OAuth callback error param, open).

borrow: Per-network tabs seeded from a 'Main' draft (Nootti) and side-by-side live previews per network with auto thread-splitting at each network's limit (Bluestodon). This is the single most-praised composer UX in the space and is cheap to build in Flutter.

Pre-flight media validation per provider before publishing (Postiz issue #1262 'MediaCapabilities' request; Buffer refuses Instagram hand-off when aspect ratio is wrong). Validate size/aspect/duration/count locally and show why a network is greyed out.

Postiz Bluesky provider's arm -> confirm -> publish handshake to make retries idempotent and avoid double posts after a network timeout; also its 429 handling (sleep 5s * attempt) and mapping of X 'not permitted' to a non-retryable error.

Postiz's per-provider maxLength() with a 'Verified' flag read at connect time (280 vs 4,000 on X), and Bluesky's RichText.detectFacets() for links/mentions; Postiz also shrinks images iteratively to fit Bluesky's ~976KB blob cap and enforces 4 images / 1 video.

Mixpost's X cost-control switches (analytics history window, engagement reads on/off, 'posts with links' per thread) - with pay-per-use X pricing since Feb 2026, let users cap what Crier may spend and default to write-only.

Mixpost/Postiz both require a *public HTTPS* redirect for Meta/TikTok. Crier should document which networks accept loopback (127.0.0.1) redirects and, for those that do not, offer the hand-off route instead of pretending.

Truthful 'tiers' per network in the UI, copied from Postiz TikTok docs: 'unaudited app => private-only posts, max 5 users/24h', 'Instagram testers-only until app review', 'LinkedIn refresh needs Advertising API form'. Show these as badges on the account card so users understand BYOK limits before they start.

Buffer-style notification publishing as a first-class network type: schedule locally, fire a local notification, copy caption to clipboard, hand the first image to the app via share intent/URL scheme and save the rest to the gallery. Use the documented Instagram routes: Android ACTION_SEND with EXTRA_STREAM (JPEG/GIF/PNG; MP4/MKV 3s-10min, min 640x640) to package com.instagram.android; Stories via com.instagram.share.ADD_TO_STORY (Android) / instagram-stories://share?source_application=<FB App ID> (iOS, pasteboard key com.instagram.sharedSticker.backgroundImage) - a Facebook App ID is mandatory since Jan 2023. Captions cannot be prefilled on either platform; clipboard is the only option.

Flare's expired-session UX: a toast with a 'log in again' button targeted at the one expired account (issue #2160), plus clearing WebView cache/history/form data on every fresh login screen (#2154/#2161) if Crier ever ships a WebView login.
Linus2punkt0's visibility mapping table (Mastodon 'who can view' vs Bluesky/X 'who can interact') and quote-post fallback (convert to reply or append URL) when a target lacks the feature.
tootify's zero-UI selection trick (only cross-post what you self-liked) could become an optional 'cross-post only when I tag it' rule in Crier.
mastodon-to-bluesky's IGNORE_TAGS and a configurable BLUESKY_MAX_POST_LENGTH show users want simple per-target rules; keep rules declarative.

AndStatus and Postiz both separate 'account' from 'network app credentials'; Postiz issue #2120 / #1016 ask for multiple app credentials per instance - Crier's per-user BYOK already solves this; advertise it.

Positioning: every OSS tool that is serverless (Flare, Fread, AndStatus) only supports open protocols or reverse-engineered X; every tool supporting Instagram/TikTok/LinkedIn (Postiz, Mixpost Pro) is a server with a reviewed app. Crier's honest niche: local-first + open protocols via official APIs + hand-off for closed networks + optional BYOK for X/Threads/LinkedIn.
Bridge-awareness: detect if the user's Mastodon account is bridged via Bridgy Fed and warn that cross-posting to Bluesky would create duplicates.
pitfalls: X API shutdowns killed an entire generation of crossposters: moa.party stopped 2023-02-28, renatolond's crossposter archived 2023-05-26 after its elevated limits were silently revoked (capped to 300 statuses/3h), Twidere stopped logging in Feb 2023, AndStatus removed Twitter in v61.00 ('no free access to reading tweets anymore'). Design Crier so a network can be removed/disabled without breaking the app.

X moved again in 2026: Postiz issue #1354 (Mar-Apr 2026) - after X's console migration, maintainers tell users to 'migrate the application to the new developer console at console.x.com' and 'if the app uses the Free tier, create a new app with Pay-as-you-go pricing and add credits'. Mixpost's current X guide only covers 'Pay as you go' and keeps a 'legacy' free-tier page. Expect every user's X app to need recreation and expect posting to cost money.

X app-type gotcha: Postiz requires 'Native App' for OAuth 1.0a (else error 32) while Mixpost requires 'Web App, Automated App or Bot' with OAuth 1.0a keys - the portal settings differ per flow; document exact portal screenshots for Crier's flow (PKCE OAuth 2.0 with tweet.write + media.write is a different setup again).

Character counting bugs are common: Mixpost #65 'Twitter/X character count is incorrect' (2 chars too long -> 'Your Tweet text is too long'), Postiz #1581 (https URLs stripped, thread replies lost), #1013 (HTML tags leaking into thread finisher). Use twitter-text weighted counting for X, graphemes for Bluesky (300), per-instance max_toot_chars for Mastodon, and test with emoji + URLs.

Meta is the hardest: Postiz #918 'Could not add provider' (open since Aug 2025, 59 comments), #1155 Instagram Standalone OAuth client_id encoding + 'Could not add provider' (Jan 2026, open), #621 'Facebook App Review?' (nobody could answer whether a single-user dev-mode app keeps advanced access; closed stale). Mixpost docs: only tester accounts can connect until the app is published, then app review for every permission. Only Professional (Business/Creator) IG accounts work.

TikTok unaudited apps can only make private (SELF_ONLY) posts for max 5 users/24h, need HTTPS redirect, verified domain, ToS + privacy URLs, and media reachable over public HTTPS - impossible for a pure local app. Treat TikTok as hand-off-only.
LinkedIn token refresh silently fails unless the 'Advertising API' product request form is approved (Postiz docs); plan for 60-day re-login otherwise.

Mixpost/Postiz model (one developer app per instance, keys in env) does not transfer to a per-user mobile app: every Crier user must create their own Meta/X/LinkedIn apps, which these projects say 'can take weeks'. Set expectations in onboarding.

Threads has no read API for clients (Openvibe's Threads account is write-only); Postiz docs say threads_content_publish needs no extra review but still needs a Meta app + 2FA on the Business account ('no business portfolios available' error). Postiz does not implement Meta's required uninstall/delete callback URLs - Crier will need placeholder endpoints or a static page.

WebView/cookie automation of X works today (Flare, twikit) but is explicitly 'reduces but doesn't eliminate the risk of account suspension'; repeated logins trigger alerts; X's web GraphQL endpoints change without notice (Flare needed multiple login fixes in 2026, Windows login broke #1381). For Instagram the same approach (instagrapi) routinely yields challenge_required/action blocks and is a ToS violation. If Crier ships it at all, isolate it behind an 'unsupported, may get your account banned' toggle and never for Instagram.

Bluesky app passwords are legacy: Bluesky told devs in Sept 2024 to stop using them for new projects; OAuth remained developer-preview through 2025 with scopes still landing (transition:email June 2025). Postiz still uses app passwords + custom PDS URL; Mixpost appears to use a generated key. Plan OAuth with loopback/custom-scheme client metadata but keep an app-password fallback for self-hosted PDSes.
Mixpost #204 (open, Jun 2026): reflected XSS through the OAuth callback 'error' parameter - sanitise anything a provider echoes back into Crier's loopback callback page.
Security hygiene for WebView logins (Flare #2154/#2161): WebView keeps cache/history/form data between accounts; clear them or users leak sessions across accounts.

Instagram hand-off cannot prefill captions (Meta docs for Sharing to Feed and Stories mention no text parameter; Buffer puts the caption on the clipboard). Carousels can only hand off the first image. Stories require a Facebook App ID since Jan 2023 and Android requires FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION.
Socioboard shows the failure mode of 'support nine networks' projects: only Dependabot commits since 2025. Prefer fewer networks done well.

Hosted crossposters (Skymoth 'not designed with selfhosting in mind', SkyBridge public instance rate-limited) show that a free public relay is a liability; Crier's no-server stance is a feature - keep it.

UNVERIFIED (recollection, not confirmed by a fetched page): Instagram's Android share-to-feed is commonly implemented with intent.setPackage("com.instagram.android") though Meta's doc shows createChooser(); iOS feed hand-off via instagram://library?LocalIdentifier=<PHAsset id> is widely used but is undocumented/deprecated by Meta. X Free tier numbers (500 writes/month, 17 writes/24h, 100 reads/month) come from third-party blogs, and the Feb 2026 'free tier closed / pay-per-use' change is also from blogs (socialcrawl.dev, blotato) rather than an X page. Mixpost's Bluesky 'private key' being an OAuth client key is inferred. bluesky-crossposter and tootify licenses were not retrievable.
